newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND TAKE HONOURS ON 1ST DAY VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND TAKE HONOURS ON 1ST DAY VS NZ.

text.p: England took first-day honours in the third and final cricket test against New Zealand at Lancaster Park on Friday.
Having won the toss and sent New Zealand in to bat, England bowled well to have the homeside on 229 for five at stumps, just one wicket shy of its long tailend.

Adam Parore was on 38 and allrounder Chris Cairns was on 10. New Zealand, who trail England 0-1 after losing in the second test in Wellington, twice looked to be establishing sound platforms in their search for a series-equalling win.
Opener Blair Pocock and new cap Matt Horne added 64 for the second wicket and stand-in captain Stephen Fleming and Parore put on the same amount for the fifth wicket.
But England broke both partnerships just as they began to look ominous.
Horne batted impressively on his debut for 42 before the fast-medium Darren Gough enticed him to play at an outswinging ball and he was well caught by Graham Thorpe at first slip.

Fleming, who became New Zealand's youngest test skipper when regular captain Lee Germon was ruled out by a groin strain, was in full flight when offspinner Robert Croft drew him down the pitch for Alec Stewart to make a smart stumping.
Fleming was out for 62, his 11th test 50.
Croft was the pick of the England attack, taking three for 49 off 24 overs, while fast-medium Dominic Cork and Gough took one wicket each.
Horne's day ended badly when an X-ray revealed he had fractured a bone in his left hand. He was struck by a ball from Gough early in his innings.
Horne will not field during England's innings but is expected to be able to bat in New Zealand's second innings later in the test.
